8: From variant to mechanism to medicine in four documented stages, each a case-agnostic tool with a provenance manifest. (1) Hand-off: Track 1's confirmed compound-heterozygous BUB1B pair (a stop allele + a kinase-region missense, trans configuration confirmed by the challenge's answer key) was written into a structured 'mechanism card' (ressources/track2/mechanism.json): gene, protein, the two allele classes (never positions), loss-of-function reading, the spindle-assembly-checkpoint pathway, downstream consequences, the tumour context (rhabdomyosarcoma) from the clinical terms, and four repurposing directions with seed genes - D1 reinforce the checkpoint, D2 exploit aneuploidy stress, D3 stabilise the remaining BubR1 (hypomorph), D4 the child's tumour. Iteration 2's measured genotype facts (allele dosage from the raw reads, exon copy number, structural-variant absence, the missense's position in the protein, pathogenicity lanes, P(trans)) were appended as a card revision (v3), with the aneuploidy burden marked unmeasured. (2) Search: the card's seeds were expanded through Reactome pathways to 277 targets; Open Targets, ChEMBL and DGIdb returned 3,859 drug-target rows and 359 market-approved drugs; openFDA confirmed US labels; ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed answered trial and literature questions, all queries derived from the card. (3) Grading: every approved drug on every direction was placed on a five-rung evidence ladder pre-registered before the search (5 approved for a related indication with paediatric use; 4 trial in a related indication; 3 animal model of the mechanism; 2 cell model; 1 mechanism only - named, never submitted). Automated tests (approval, label and its Pediatric Use section, tumour-context trials, studies admitting children, PubMed co-mention counts) and curated tests (one PubMed paper per row, read by a person, 13 rows) are printed side by side; inherited class-level evidence is marked 'proxy'. Six falsifiable claims (one per direction, one for the control, one for paediatric data) were registered with predictions and refutation conditions before any drug-level query. (4) Control: the same pipeline ran on two decoy cards - the child's clinical side kept, the gene swapped (NTRK3 by a seeded draw from Track 1's decoy set; XDH, an unrelated metabolic enzyme). This is a negative control in the usual sense: an input the pipeline should not be able to argue from, run through the unchanged code so that whatever comes out for the decoy as readily as for BUB1B is attributed to database density or the clinical queries rather than to the mechanism. A direction whose approved drugs overlap a decoy's at Jaccard >= 0.10 is reported as non-specific; D4 did (0.25) and is argued only from curated mechanism results. Output: 11 drugs with a cited mechanism result (statins; niacin/nicotinamide; chloroquine; bortezomib, metformin, valproic acid, vorinostat, hydroxychloroquine, atorvastatin), 50 drugs already in rhabdomyosarcoma trials listed as such, and a 23-drug do-not table (spindle poisons, checkpoint inhibitors, standard of care).
9: Both, kept apart and printed side by side. Automated: drug-target database queries (Open Targets, ChEMBL, DGIdb, Reactome, openFDA, ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed E-utilities) driven by the mechanism card, plus per-drug PubMed co-mention counts and paediatric-trial lookups; these produce the candidate set and the automated rungs 4-5. Manual: the evidence rungs 2-3 come from 13 papers read by a person and entered in evidence.tsv with the PubMed id, the model (cell / in vivo) and a proxy flag when the paper tested a same-axis compound rather than the approved drug. LLM assistance was used to draft queries, code and prose; every PubMed id was resolved live against E-utilities before it was written down, and four ids first recalled from memory were wrong and replaced by title search before entering any file.
10: Thirteen curated rows, each one cited result: Tang & Amon 2011 (PMID 21315436) - chloroquine and the AMPK activator AICAR are aneuploidy-selective in trisomic and aneuploid cells (rung 2 for chloroquine; metformin and hydroxychloroquine inherit as proxies); Ippolito 2024 (39247952) and Chui 2019 (31530568) - aneuploid cells depend on protein degradation and are more sensitive to proteasome inhibition (bortezomib, class proxy); North 2014 (24825348) - the NAD+ precursor NMN raised BubR1 in vivo and SIRT2 extended the lifespan of BubR1-hypomorphic mice (rung 3; niacin and nicotinamide as proxies); Park 2017 (28985013) and Choi 2009 (19407811) - HDAC2/3 deacetylation drives BubR1 degradation, acetylation protects it (valproic acid, vorinostat as class proxies); Gizaw 2025 (41249736) - lovastatin itself reduced rhabdomyosarcoma cell proliferation and cholesterol synthesis is a non-redundant tumour vulnerability (rung 2; simvastatin and atorvastatin as proxies). The anti-directions rest on Suijkerbuijk 2010 (20516114, MVA cells have a weakened checkpoint), Sinha 2019 (30601084, mitotic slippage) and Cohen-Sharir 2021 (33505028, aneuploid cells are killed by checkpoint inhibition). The mechanism section rests on Hanks 2004 (15475955) and Suijkerbuijk 2010. Curation was one person's reading of the abstracts on 2026-09-18; every row carries its PubMed id so it can be checked.
11: Publicly available sources only. No proprietary data source was used.
12: Open Targets Platform (GraphQL API, drugAndClinicalCandidates per target and disease), ChEMBL (REST: target search, mechanism, molecule max_phase, first approval, ATC), DGIdb (GraphQL interactions), Reactome ContentService (pathways containing the protein, participants), openFDA drug labels (current US label; the pediatric_use section), ClinicalTrials.gov v2 (studies by condition and intervention; aggFilters=ages:child for studies admitting children), PubMed E-utilities (esearch counts and ids, esummary), plus ClinVar (the stop allele's classification) and gnomAD (population absence of the missense) from Track 1. DrugBank was named by the form but not queried: its programmatic access needs a licence. Every reply is cached and its digest rolled into the table's manifest; retrieval dates are 2026-09-05 (first snapshot) and 2026-09-18 (refresh and enrichment).
14: Loss of function, hypomorphic, of a confirmed compound heterozygote. One allele is a stop change in exon 17 of 23 (ClinVar pathogenic / likely pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1): no functional BubR1 from that copy. The other is a missense change in the last exon: absent from gnomAD, AlphaMissense likely-pathogenic (log-likelihood-ratio lane 4.33), CADD 24.5, sitting outside every InterPro domain-typed entry in a region AlphaFold models at pLDDT 91 - a weakened copy, not a dead one, consistent with every published MVA1 genotype (complete loss is embryonic-lethal). No gain-of-function or dominant-negative activity is reported for BUB1B. Trans configuration: confirmed by the oracle's full match at rank 1 (population phasing was undetermined; read-backed phase blocks did not reach the gene). Dosage: both alleles at one-copy multiplicity in the raw reads by an alignment-free k-mer method; every exon at two copies; no structural variant in the gene. Pathway: the spindle assembly checkpoint - BubR1 is a core component of the mitotic checkpoint complex that inhibits APC/C-CDC20 and recruits PP2A-B56 to kinetochores; less BubR1 gives a leaky checkpoint (Suijkerbuijk 2010 measured strongly reduced BubR1 and a weakened checkpoint in MVA cells). Downstream: premature anaphase and chromosome missegregation; mosaic variegated aneuploidy; proteotoxic and metabolic stress in aneuploid cells; cancer predisposition (rhabdomyosarcoma - the child's presenting tumour - Wilms tumour, leukaemia); growth restriction and nephrocalcinosis, which are the delivered clinical terms. Stated gaps: the aneuploid fraction in this child's sample is unmeasured (the karyotype statistic run had no power for mosaic gains; the powered analysis is planned), and whether the missense copy is unstable or catalytically inactive is open - so direction D3 is argued as raising BubR1 abundance, not as refolding it.
15: Roughly four working days across two people-equivalents: one day for the mechanism card and the data layer (iteration 1, 2026-09-05/06), and about three days on 2026-09-18 for the card revision, the six pre-registered claims, the enrichment adapters and ladder, the decoy control, the curation, the figures, the dashboard page and this report. Compute and cost: a laptop, two runs of about ten minutes each (the snapshot and the enrichment) against seven public APIs, most of that runtime spent waiting politely between per-drug requests rather than computing; seconds on a re-run once the replies are cached. No cloud, no GPU, no cluster, no paid data source and no licence fee - the only cost that does not shrink on a second case is the person-read curation (13 abstracts, one reader, one day).
16: Question. Given a confirmed compound-heterozygous loss of BUB1B (a stop allele and a hypomorphic kinase-region missense) in a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy and rhabdomyosarcoma, which market-approved drugs act on the mechanism, and how strong is the evidence for each? Method. A structured mechanism card written from Track 1's confirmed result and iteration 2's measured genotype facts drives every query: Reactome expands the card's seed genes to 277 targets; Open Targets, ChEMBL and DGIdb return 359 approved drugs; openFDA, ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed answer label, trial and literature questions per drug. Every approved drug on every direction is placed on a five-rung evidence ladder pre-registered before the search (approved with paediatric use; trial in a related indication; animal model; cell model; mechanism only), with the automated tests and the 13 person-curated PubMed rows printed side by side and inherited class-level evidence flagged as proxy. Six claims were registered with refutation conditions before any drug-level query. The whole pipeline ran unchanged on two decoy cards (same child, gene swapped for NTRK3 and for XDH) as a specificity control. Results. Direction D1 (reinforce the checkpoint) has no approved drug and became the do-not table. D2 (aneuploidy stress): chloroquine has a molecule-level cell result; metformin, hydroxychloroquine and bortezomib inherit class-level results. D3 (raise BubR1): NAD+ repletion raised BubR1 in BubR1-hypomorphic mice, inherited by niacin and nicotinamide (rung 3); HDAC inhibitors act on BubR1's acetylation switch at class level. D4 (the tumour): lovastatin itself slowed rhabdomyosarcoma cells, and a completed paediatric phase-1 trial gave simvastatin with chemotherapy in relapsed solid tumours including rhabdomyosarcoma. Eleven drugs carry a cited mechanism result; fifty more reach the top rung only because they are already in rhabdomyosarcoma trials and are listed as such, not claimed. The decoy control showed D4's automated stage is non-specific (Jaccard 0.25 against NTRK3) while D1-D3 are gene-specific, and it exposed a grading flaw (tumour trials lifting mechanism directions) that was corrected before any verdict, with the change recorded. The do-not table names 13 spindle poisons - including standard rhabdomyosarcoma chemotherapy - as a caution for the treating team, because those drugs rely on the very checkpoint that is weakened, and no approved checkpoint inhibitor exists. Strengths. Pre-registration; a decoy control for a repurposing pipeline; automated and curated evidence never merged silently; complete lineage (manifests, warehouse edges); case-agnostic tooling (swap the card, run another case); no patient data in any Track 2 artifact. Limitations. Curated rungs are one reader's; rung 3 is a single mouse paper; the child's aneuploid fraction is unmeasured; the missense's unstable-versus-inactive status is open; DrugBank was not queried; a paediatric pointer is not safety data. These are hypotheses for follow-up, not evidence that any medicine works.
